# A late-registered workspace gains no recovery button until a reload

## Context

This exists because it blocked a different decision, which is the useful part of its provenance.

`#18553` adds a Workstation reset-to-default. When a pane has been torn into its own OS window, the reset reclaims it into the shipped document and leaves the vessel **embodied** — a live window holding an empty document. The alternative was to retire that vessel in the same act, which is what the engine's own transfer path does when a transfer empties its source (`retireReturnedVessel`).

@neo-opus-vega ruled against retirement, and the reason is this ticket: **retirement is only invertible if the recovery affordance exists warm, and it does not.** Reset is one undoable history row. Undo of a reset restores the item into a retired vessel's document, and per ADR 0029 nothing may auto-spawn a window to re-embody it — re-embodiment is a user gesture through the topology bar's `Open workstation-vessel:<item> as window` button. That button is populated once, at boot. So a user who resets and then undoes is left holding a pane in a workspace they cannot reopen without a reload.

Order matters and is the whole shape of this ticket: **membership signal first, retirement behind it.**

## The Problem

`Workstation.view.WorkspaceController#syncTopologyBar` fills the topology bar's per-workspace recovery buttons from live Group membership. Its own docblock already asks the engine for what is missing, verbatim:

> Idempotent and re-callable, but wired to `onComponentConstructed` alone — the same single population the previous shape performed. `WorkspaceSet` publishes no membership signal, so a participant registered after boot still gains no buttons until a reload; that is unchanged here and needs a signal in the engine, not a second reader in this file.

That is a self-authored contract note, so it is evidence of intent, not of the engine's state. The engine's state was checked separately and agrees: `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.WorkspaceSet` (`src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs`) exposes `register` (`:234`) and `unregister` (`:382`) and has **no** event, fire, publish, notify or observable-config surface anywhere in the class. Membership changes are therefore unobservable by construction, not merely unsubscribed.

The user-visible consequence today: pop a pane out warm and the bar offers no way to reopen that vessel after it closes, for the remainder of the session. A reload fixes it, which is the tell that the data is right and only the notification is absent.

## The Architectural Reality

- `WorkspaceSet` is the keyed registry the Group commits through — `register` / `unregister` / `has` / `getDocument` / `commit` / `transfer` / `write`. It owns membership and publishes nothing about it.
- `WorkspaceController#syncTopologyBar` is the only reader, reaching the view-declared bar through its reference and supplying only the membership-dependent part. It is already idempotent and re-callable, so the consumer side of this is a subscription, not a rewrite.
- The controller's docblock explicitly rejects the cheap fix — "needs a signal in the engine, not a second reader in this file". A second reader would be a poll or a second lifecycle hook, and either re-derives membership the registry already knows.
- The engine's own precedent for this shape is a reactive config observed by the subscriber, not an event listener: tying cleanup to the subscriber's lifetime is what keeps a controller from leaking past its component.
- Vessel re-embodiment routes through `?workspace=<key>` and the owner's `connect` adoption. That path is proven working **cold** (a real-window witness on a fresh boot); only the warm affordance is missing.

## The Fix

**Step 1 — the engine publishes membership.** Give `WorkspaceSet` an observable membership surface that `register` and `unregister` update, carrying enough for a consumer to render an affordance per participant (the workspace key, and whether it is the main workspace). A reactive config the subscriber observes is the shape to prefer over an event emitter, so cleanup binds to the subscriber.

**Step 2 — the consumer subscribes.** `WorkspaceController` observes that surface and re-runs `syncTopologyBar`, replacing the `onComponentConstructed`-only wiring. The method is already idempotent, and its docblock's limitation paragraph is deleted in the same diff — a documented limitation outliving its cause is the decay this repo's guards exist to stop.

**Step 3 — retirement becomes eligible, as a separate deliverable.** Only once the bar re-syncs warm does retiring an emptied vessel on reset become invertible, at which point `#18553`'s deferred branch can be reconsidered on its merits. Explicitly **not** in this ticket's scope: this ticket earns the option, it does not exercise it.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WorkspaceSet` membership surface (**new**) | ADR 0029 §2 registry ownership | Updated by `register`/`unregister`; observable by a consumer | None needed — additive; no existing consumer reads membership reactively today | Class JSDoc + the ADR if the contract is normative | Verified absent: no `fire`/`on`/`publish`/`notify`/`observeConfig` in `src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs`; `register` at `:234`, `unregister` at `:382` |
| `WorkspaceController#syncTopologyBar` | Its own docblock, quoted above | Re-runs on membership change instead of at construction only | Construction-time population remains the first call, so a non-publishing engine degrades to today's behaviour | Docblock's limitation paragraph deleted with its cause | Verified present and idempotent at `apps/workstation/view/WorkspaceController.mjs`; single call site in `onComponentConstructed` |
| Topology bar recovery buttons | View-declared structure, controller-supplied contents | One per non-main participant, gained and lost warm | Absent buttons, i.e. today | Covered by the bar's own contract | Cold path proven by a real-window witness; warm path is the gap |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029`. The ADR's "restore never auto-spawns a window" rule is what makes a *user-gesture* affordance load-bearing rather than optional, so publishing membership serves that rule rather than challenging it. If the membership surface is written as a normative registry contract rather than an implementation detail, that is an `amends` and the amendment lands first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorkspaceSet.register` and `unregister` make membership observable, asserted by a unit arm that subscribes and counts notifications for both directions.
- [ ] A participant registered **after** boot gains its recovery button without a reload, asserted through the controller rather than by reading the registry.
- [ ] An unregistered participant loses its button — the arm covers removal, not only addition, since a stale affordance that opens a dead workspace is worse than an absent one.
- [ ] The subscription is torn down with its subscriber: a destroyed controller receives no notification and leaks no handler, asserted directly.
- [ ] `syncTopologyBar`'s docblock limitation paragraph is removed in the same diff that removes its cause.
- [ ] Mutation-verified: reverting the publication reds the late-registration arm specifically, and the red is shown to fail on the affordance assertion rather than on fixture or boot.
- [ ] A construction-time population still happens, so the first paint is unchanged — a control arm, since this is the behaviour most likely to be traded away by accident.

## Out of Scope

- Retiring an emptied vessel on reset. That is the option this ticket earns; exercising it is a separate deliverable against `#18553`'s deferred branch.
- The live-pane-does-not-follow defect (#18621). Unrelated tier, and it is not a prerequisite in either direction.
- Any change to `?workspace=<key>` routing or the `connect` adoption path, which a witness proved working cold.
- Park/restore gesture machinery (`#18533`).

## Avoided Traps

- **A second reader in the consumer.** A poll or an extra lifecycle hook re-derives what the registry already knows, and the controller's docblock names this as the wrong fix before anyone proposed it.
- **An event emitter over a reactive config.** `.on()` leaks past the subscriber; an observed config ties cleanup to the observer's lifetime. The AC asserting teardown exists to keep this honest.
- **Retiring first and adding the affordance later.** That is the ordering that strands a user mid-undo, and it is exactly what the fork rejected.

## Related

- `#18553` / `#18595` — the reset that surfaced this; its body records the fork and this ticket as the prerequisite for the branch it declined.
- `#18532` / `#18533` — vessel lifecycle and park/restore, adjacent and not on this path.
- #18621 — the live-pane defect from the same witness, independent of this.
